findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, not per instance
findings.body:
`queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain dataclass default. Python evaluates it once, when the class is defined at module import.

As a result, every `AssignmentSource` created via `from_integration()` or `from_dict()` without an explicit `queued` gets the same timestamp: the moment the web or worker process imported the module. That can be hours or days old. Any future use of `queued` (staleness checks, ordering of rapid assignment changes, debugging/logging) will silently get wrong data.

`test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so it does not catch this.

Fix: use `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: Cycle check is per-integration, so other linked issues in the same integration stop syncing
findings.body:
`should_sync` returns False whenever `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`. The task runs once per linked ExternalIssue, but the check ignores which external issue triggered the change.

If a Sentry group is linked to two issues in the same Jira integration (e.g. APP-1 and APP-2), a webhook assigning APP-1 updates the Sentry assignee. The outbound sync to APP-2 is then skipped too, because it shares the integration id. Before this change APP-2 would have received the new assignee, so this silently regresses assignee propagation.

The nearby comment says other targets should still get the change, but that only holds across different integrations, not across different issues in one integration.

Fix: carry the originating external issue (key or id) in `AssignmentSource` and skip only that external issue.

findings.title: Task kwargs now contain a raw `datetime` object
findings.body:
`assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict`, so the `queued` value passed to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` is a `datetime` instance. This works only under pickle (or serializer-specific datetime handling).

Under plain JSON task serialization, which Sentry is moving toward, it will either fail to serialize or arrive as a string. `from_dict` then passes that string straight into the dataclass without parsing, leaving `queued` as a `str` despite its `datetime` annotation.

Fix: serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. isoformat or epoch) in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: `sync_status_outbound` abstract signature changed but never wired up
No test covers the actual inbound→outbound cycle or other-integration propagation
findings.body:
The new test calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly with an `AssignmentSource`. Nothing verifies the real fix path, i.e. that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (assign and deassign), run under `self.tasks()`, does not enqueue an outbound sync back to the originating integration.

There is also no test that a different integration linked to the same group still receives the outbound assignee sync when the source is another integration. The PR description explicitly claims that behavior.

`test_assignee_sync_inbound_assign` and `test_assignee_sync_inbound_deassign` run without `self.tasks()` and without asserting on outbound calls, so a regression in the source propagation would go unnoticed.
